First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta =2{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta +1).
$$

Letting $\theta =3x$, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡3x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡6x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}(3-2{cosh}^{2}⁡3x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}(3-2\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡6x+1))\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}(3-\operatorname{cosh}⁡6x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}(2-\operatorname{cosh}⁡6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(2x-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sinh}⁡6x)|}_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =[2\cdot \frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(6\cdot \frac{1}{2})]-[2\cdot 0-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(6\cdot 0)] \\  & =1-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{sinh}⁡3.\end{aligned}
$$
